items.title: Temporal point-process models and conditional intensity
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as in [[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]]. Fix a finite horizon $T>0$, a probability space with an increasing filtration $(\mathcal F_t)$ in the all-pairs convention of [[def-continuous-time-filtration-and-all-pairs-martingale]], and an adapted càdlàg (right-continuous with left limits), nondecreasing, integer-valued process $N$ with $N_0=0$, $N_T<\infty$ almost surely, and jumps $\Delta N_t\in\{0,1\}$ outside one null event. Such a process is **simple**: its event times are strictly ordered, $0<T_1<\cdots<T_{N_T}\le T$. It is **locally finite** when it has finitely many events on every finite interval. For conditional-law calculations, the model supplies a measurable history space $(\mathsf H,\mathcal G)$, an adapted measurable history random element $H_t$ recording the initial information and events observed through time $t$, and a measurable update map $h\mapsto h\oplus u$ that appends an event at time $u$. Write $\mathcal H_t:=\sigma(H_t)$ and let $H_{t-}$ record only events strictly before $t$. Relevant exogenous covariates are included in the supplied history. Measurability has the meaning of [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]. Predictability is measurability for the predictable sigma-algebra generated by $(s,u]\times A$ with $A\in\mathcal F_s$ and the time-zero generators, as in [[def-progressively-measurable-and-predictable-process]]. The model supplies a probability kernel $K_{t,h}$ on $(t,\infty]$ for the next event time given history $h$ at time $t$ ([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]], [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]); its finite-time density versions are jointly measurable in $(t,h,u)$. The value $+\infty$ means that no later event occurs. If the finite-time measure is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure ([[def-absolutely-continuous-with-respect-to-a-positive-measure]], [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]], [[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]), let $f_{t,h}$ be its supplied nonnegative Radon--Nikodym density ([[def-radon-nikodym-derivative]]). Write $S_{t,h}(u):=K_{t,h}((u,\infty])$ for its survivor and define its **no-event conditional hazard** by $$ \lambda_{t,h}^*(u):=\frac{f_{t,h}(u)}{S_{t,h}(u)} \qquad\text{where }S_{t,h}(u)>0. $$ Assume these hazards are locally integrable on every finite interval. The associated process value $\lambda^*(u):=\lambda_{u,H_{u-}}^*(u)$ is required to have a nonnegative predictable version. This pre-event convention means the event at $u$ does not change its own intensity. The **temporal conditional-intensity model** requires both this hazard-compatible conditional law and the separate counting-process compensator contract of [[def-counting-process-intensity-and-compensator-contract]]: if an at-risk indicator $Y$ and intensity density $\lambda$ are separately specified, the effective intensity is $\lambda^*=Y\lambda$; without an at-risk indicator, it is $\lambda^*$. Then $A_t=\int_0^t\lambda^*(u)\,du$ is finite pathwise, continuous, adapted and predictable, $\mathbb E[A_T]<\infty$, and $N-A$ is a square-integrable martingale in the all-pairs convention of [[def-continuous-time-adapted-process-and-martingale]]. At-risk exposure, if present, is part of the effective intensity. The compensator clause is a model assumption: a displayed hazard formula alone proves neither that a process with this law exists nor that the martingale contract holds. No stationarity or non-explosion claim follows from writing an intensity specification.

items.title: Inter-event survival and density from a conditional intensity
items.statement: Fix a supplied event history $h$ at time $t$ in the model of [[def-temporal-point-process-and-conditional-intensity]]. Let $\lambda_h^*(u)$ be its nonnegative no-event conditional hazard, supplied as a locally integrable version on every finite interval, and put $$ \Lambda_h(u):=\int_t^u\lambda_h^*(s)\,ds. $$ For each finite $U>t$, on $t\le u\le U$ the conditional survivor and finite- time density of the next event are $$ S_h(u)=\exp(-\Lambda_h(u)),\qquad f_h(u)=\lambda_h^*(u)\exp(-\Lambda_h(u)) \quad\text{for almost every }u. $$ If $\Lambda_h(u)\to\Lambda_h(\infty)<\infty$ as $u\to\infty$, then $K_h(\{\infty\})=\exp(-\Lambda_h(\infty))$. If $\Lambda_h(u)\to\infty$, this terminal mass is zero. These conclusions concern one next-event law and do not prove non-explosion of an entire process.

items.title: Finite-window homogeneous Poisson construction and ordered event-time density
items.statement: Let $T>0$, $\theta>0$, and let $S=(0,T]$ carry its subspace topology and Borel sigma-algebra. This space is Hausdorff as a subspace of $\mathbb R$; rational intervals give a countable base; and each $x\in S$ has a compact neighborhood $[x-\delta,x+\delta]\cap S$ for some $0<\delta<x$. Let $\ell$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to $S$. There exists a Poisson point process on $S$ with intensity measure $\nu_\theta(B)=\theta\ell(B)$. Its total count is finite almost surely, its event times have no ties almost surely, and for every integer $m\ge0$ the joint density of the ordered event times $$ 0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T,\qquad N(S)=m, $$ with respect to $m$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on the ordered simplex is $$ e^{-\theta T}\theta^m. $$ For $m>0$, conditional on $N(S)=m$, the ordered event times have density $m!/T^m$. For $m=0$ the empty-pattern probability is $e^{-\theta T}$.

items.title: Conditional-intensity inter-event law and point-pattern likelihood
items.statement: Assume AC, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice for the cited likelihood and hazard-calculus interfaces. Fix $T>0$ and a common specified initial history. Let $(P_\theta)$ be a supplied family of laws for actual simple, non-explosive temporal point-process models on $(0,T]$ satisfying [[def-temporal-point-process-and-conditional-intensity]], with jointly measurable conditional history-update and waiting-time kernels. Let $P_0$ be the supplied unit-rate Poisson reference on the finite-pattern space $$ \mathsf X_T=\bigsqcup_{m\ge0}\Delta_m,\qquad \Delta_0=\{\varnothing\},\quad \Delta_m=\{(t_1,\ldots,t_m):0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T\}, $$ equipped with the disjoint-union Borel sigma-algebra. For a pattern $0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$, let $h_{i-1}$ be the initial history updated by $t_1,\ldots,t_{i-1}$. On each simplex, the laws are dominated by $P_0$ and the following chosen density representative gives the Radon–Nikodym derivative $P_0$-almost everywhere: $$ \frac{dP_\theta}{dP_0}(t_1,\ldots,t_m) =e^T\left(\prod_{i=1}^m \lambda_\theta^*(t_i\mid h_{i-1})\right) \exp\!\left(-\int_0^T\lambda_\theta^*(u\mid h_{u-})\,du\right). $$ Here $h_{u-}$ is the history immediately before $u$. Thus the likelihood as a function of $\theta$ is proportional to the product of pre-event intensities times the terminal integrated-hazard factor; $e^T$ is parameter-independent. If an observed event has zero intensity, the density is zero; a finite log-likelihood requires positive intensity at each observed event. For $m=0$, the event product is the empty product $1$ and the terminal no-event factor remains. For marked patterns, let marks lie in a supplied measurable space with a common mark probability measure $Q$. If each event has a supplied conditional mark density $q_\theta(k_i\mid t_i,h_{i-1})$ relative to $Q$, and the reference uses independent marks with law $Q$, multiply the displayed ratio by $\prod_iq_\theta(k_i\mid t_i,h_{i-1})$. The ground intensity does not determine a mark law.

items.title: A finite-window Poisson process that terminates at time one
items.statement: Let $\eta$ be a supplied Poisson point process on $(0,1]$ with Lebesgue intensity, and extend it by zero after time $1$. Its counting process is $N_t=\eta((0,t\wedge1])$. The effective conditional intensity is $\lambda^*(t)=\mathbf1_{(0,1]}(t)$ and its compensator is $A_t=t\wedge1$. This is a non-explosive process that has ended by time one, yet from the empty history the next-event law puts probability $e^{-1}$ on no event ever.

items.title: Homogeneous Poisson likelihood and a Hawkes intensity specification
items.statement: **Homogeneous Poisson case.** Let $\eta$ be a supplied homogeneous Poisson process of rate $\theta\ge0$ on $(0,T]$, with $T>0$, and let $m=N_T$ be the observed count. The likelihood ratio against the unit-rate Poisson reference is $e^T\theta^m e^{-\theta T}$, with $0^0:=1$, so the parameter-dependent likelihood is $\theta^m e^{-\theta T}$. Over the parameter space $\theta\ge0$, the maximum-likelihood estimate is $m/T$ when $m>0$ and $0$ when $m=0$. **Hawkes specification.** For parameters $\mu>0$, $\alpha\ge0$, and $\beta>0$, consider the pre-event-history intensity specification $$ \lambda^*(u)=\mu+\alpha\sum_{t_j<u}e^{-\beta(u-t_j)}. $$ For any supplied non-explosive law whose conditional hazards and separate compensator contract satisfy the temporal model with this specification, and any compatible event pattern $0<t_1<\cdots<t_m\le T$, the likelihood ratio is $$ e^T \left(\prod_{i=1}^m\left(\mu+\alpha\sum_{j<i} e^{-\beta(t_i-t_j)}\right)\right) \exp\!\left[-\mu T-\frac{\alpha}{\beta} \sum_{i=1}^m\left(1-e^{-\beta(T-t_i)}\right)\right]. $$ This is a finite-pattern likelihood calculation conditional on a compatible law. Writing the candidate specification does not prove that such a law exists, is non-explosive, or is stationary.
